citations.assessment: The sudden death scene expressly gives the name or term Zuga with the singular verb tana.
The Bavli identifies Chavor with Hadayav in its list of places. The Arukh’s Chadyav form remains separately sourced.
The checked witness has Zuga of Chadyav and singular verbs in the report.
Rashi expressly explains this as two Torah scholars from that place.
The checked Ein Yaakov has Zuga in the same sudden-death episode. Its text here does not itself give the two-scholars gloss.
The letter to Rava explicitly uses singular came with the word for a pair from Rakkat.
Rashi directly explains the pair as two Torah scholars.
The adjacent lemma identifies Rakkat as Tiberias.
Tosafot explicitly quotes Arukh’s name-of-a-sage explanation, with a different headword form.
The Yerushalmi gives Rabbi, rather than Rava, and expressly says two pairs in the parallel version. The singular verb and the plural pronoun are both present.
